english_verification.review_scope: Read the A77 history template, opening Orda Aldresia mission block, native country-name localisation, selected current English flavour text on its singing blade/gunblade and Prodigal Son, plus the Second Son event block implementing the occupied-country vassalisation and ruler/heir killings. Read three chunks from the same dedicated Orda Aldresia Wiki page: Religion(s), History, and Greentide Schism. The latter confirms the 1424 context and that some young knights left for Escann. This is representative terminology/history checking, not a full narrative or mission-tree audit. Primary compared all native idea names/descriptions by actual current English localisation key. Source ranges may be locator envelopes; conditional and predecessor idea sets remain separate. No formal validators, tests, builds or browser checks were run.
unresolved: The Wiki passage supports organisation background and selected history, not all current mission mechanics or later outcomes.
A77 to Z97 is a conditional event/choice route; the successor's full endgame was outside this bounded review.
The exact scope and reachability of all discussed player-experience routes were not exhaustively audited.

rationale.campaign_length: The 19 A77-exclusive missions alone do not capture the campaign length because a conditional Z97 successor phase can follow.
rationale.colonization: The reviewed main route has no overseas-colonization focus.
rationale.complexity: Imperial support, equipment, technology, and a religious mission-tree change must be coordinated.
rationale.dark_story: Killing an occupied ruler and heir and installing a puppet are concrete dark acts.
rationale.difficulty: Mission prerequisites and political relationships add difficulty; no hands-on test was performed.
rationale.diplomacy: The Emperor's support, allies, and special political relationships constrain action.
rationale.early_pressure: The opening has significant institutional and political constraints; the country is not fully free to act.
rationale.magic_artifice_intensity: Hybrid magic, gunblades, and precursor relics form the central loop.
rationale.narrative_density: Imperial vows, civilian protection, and coercive politics create a multi-stage conflict.
rationale.tall_play: The arsenal, archive, and equipment system require investment.
rationale.trade_economy: Industry serves gunblades and arms rather than a mercantile republic.
rationale.warfare: Guardianship, shadow expeditions, and political wars run through the middle and late campaign.

identity.appearance: In 1444, an imperial arcane knightly order, theocratic state, and holder of a special political duty.
identity.formation_scope: With the A77_ravelian_option condition, flavor_orda_aldresia.48 can transfer a related country, change it to Z97, and switch its mission tree; it does not simply add Z97 missions to A77.

national_ideas.scope_note: National traditions, seven national ideas and ambition only; optional idea groups and racial/government bonuses are excluded. Conditional alternatives are separate, not stacked. Adopting new ideas depends on the actual event/decision and player choice.

description.text: “Hear my vows, Castellos, King of Gods and God of Kings, and bind me to my words as law, O lawgiver. I shall hold no lands, accept no titles, take no partner and bear no children. I shall be just and true, fair and vigilant, valiant and ardent. With your wisdom, make me an unbreakable shield, a shining sword, an indomitable fortress protecting and being guided by the dream of Anbennar. Give me the strength to fight eternal against the forces of darkness, that till my sword breaks and my light extinguishes, I can stand tall as a true Knight of Aldresia.”" With these words is one inducted into the hallowed ranks of the order. Such vows are not taken lightly and this becomes reflected in the devotion members show to their duties.

description.text: The Grandmaster of the Orda Aldresia has the distinguished privilege of acting as imperial proxy during times of peace. Beyond mediating disputes between conflicting parties within the empire, the Grandmaster also ensures imperial edicts are followed and that the rights of the various estates are being respected. This great responsibility affords the order significant sway in attracting talented aides.

description.text: The Orda Aldresia is one of the only remaining organizations that utilizes the lost art of Diranbe. Formal induction into the order requires that novitiates master the difficult task of utilizing a spellblade as their focus while engaging in melee combat. Those who are able to achieve such an undertaking are accepted and become one of the fabled arcane knights. The devastating charge of the arcane knights single handedly won many fields for the nobles during the brutal Wars of Rule.

description.text: In 1053 AA, our namesake Aldresia, led a crusade against the undead hordes and ended the White Pestilence. Aldresia and her followers were instrumental in halting one of the worst abuses wrought by magic in all of Cannorian history, thus ensuring our order remains highly respected even until this day.

description.text: The conclusion of the Wars of Rule saw the Anbennarian magocracy ousted and the nobles install Marion of the House Silmuna as Emperor. For the orders loyal service during the wars, Emperor Marion I granted the order extensive land in the eastern border territories along with the rights of imperial immediacy. This distinct right ensures that the order is exempt from paying taxes or fealty to any lord but the Emperor, thus greatly increasing our ability to raise funds and fill the coffers of Arca Aldresia.

description.text: Our privileged status as one of two sanctioned magical bodies within Anbennar affords us great prestige. This coupled with the strong military traditions of the Order ensures that we are never short of recruits from those magic users more interested in the martial applications of their gifts. Even the order's greenest recruits are able to hold their own in the field of battle under the direction of the order's masters.

description.text:
Arca Aldresia stands as a testament to the resolve and tenacity of the order. Built atop the ruins of Rotwall to commemorate the conclusion of the decades long Aldresian Crusade with the aid of the greatest abjurers and military minds of the day, the castle has evolved over the centuries into one of the most formidable fortresses in all of Anbennar.

This great citadel was able to withstand even the might of the magisters who attempted to siege it at the climax of the Wars of Rule. The humiliating defeat of the magocrats ensured continued animosity between the order and the Magisterium. Even with the advent of blackpowder, the Arca Aldresia remains nigh impregnable thanks to its multitude of magical defences and the diligence of the orders knights.

description.text:
The Ravelian Church can only be rivalled by the Jadd in their mission to spread the faith to all corners of the world.
As each Revelation is discovered (a major finding unearthed or doctrine settled within the church), the closer the faith gets to the Truth (a total understanding of the world), and the more the faith must spread bring the world to the fold.

Once the world is converted to the true faith, the Ravelians believe that God will be empowered once more and grant salvation to all.

description.text:
The Ravelian Church was born from the Ravelian Society, a group of academics and reformists that wished to unravel the secrets of the world through reason and empiricism. The first members of the society were in fact Corinites who were unconvinced that fighting injustice with sword and shield was enough, and sought for a greater fight against lies and injustice that would encompass the whole world, not just Cannor.

The Ravelian Society eventually became a place for great thinkers in a time when religious conflict and superstition was rife, and to this day their legacy of reason still permeates through the church.

description.text: The Ravelian belief in a One God is quite unique in the world of Halann. While most other faiths are polytheistic, and even the faith of Surael accepts the existence of other gods (while claiming they are dead), the Ravelian Church is truly monotheistic, believing that there is only one god. The Ravelian One God is seen as all-knowing, all-powerful and all-present - all other gods are either aspects of (a part of) God, saints that emulate God's ideal, or non-existent and false.

description.text: A type of Mechanim created by the church to serve as soldiers, guards and holy warriors. The first automata stood well above the common man, and were armed with large tower shields capable of defending their charge, in addition to an embedded gun in the other arm to fend off the unholy. Since then the Warrior Automata have become a feared reminder of what happens when religious zeal and intellectual brilliance is combined.

description.text:
"It is said that God created all things, and would bestow magic, their own power, to their creations when they deemed them worthy.
The precursor elves, one of their creations, were not worthy. And so in their envy and impatience, conspired with each other to strike down God and steal their power for themselves.

But lo, they could not defeat God truly, for God was all-powerful.
They could not find God, for God was all-present everywhere.
They could not deceive God, for God was all-knowing.

But in God's wisdom they allowed themselves to be deceived by their plot and defeated by their creations, and bound into the God Fragment.
For God has compassion and empathy for their creation, and knew that one day they may prove themselves truly worthy and redeem themselves in the eyes of the Lord."

-Provenance 1:23-30

description.text:
The Ravelian Society, and later the church, were responsible for many great advancements in the field of artificery. The Church believed that magic was divine, and that artificery was a way to allow all of God's creations to benefit from Their power (magic).

Many Rectors (the common name for a priest) were knowledgable in the art of artificery, and one of their main responsibilities was tending to the needs of the faithful, which in this case not only involved traditional religious duties, but also acting as teachers and mentors, but also as local artificers creating and repairing inventions for the needy.

description.text: Said to be the last vessel of a defeated One True God, the God Fragment is guarded in a hidden location only known to the upper echelons of the High Rectorate. The God Fragment is monitored for its rare communications, which it does through high-pitched frequencies that can be deciphered and translated into an variant of precursor elven. The High Rector and the Veridicals are the first to hear the messages of the God Fragment, and it is often up to them to discern what revelations and insights it can offer - once a new revelation is found, the High Rector acts as the speaker to evocate the God Fragment's message.

player_overview.avoid_if: Avoid this if you want unrestricted action from the start, a linear mission tree, or an uncomplicated chivalric tale.
player_overview.how_it_plays: Rebuild reputation and armaments first, confront imperial politics and shadow threats next, and choose a religious and political direction later.
player_overview.overview: The Order of Orda Aldresia once swore to guard the Emperor, but civil war and its refusal to aid those suffering in the Greentide cost it some knights. Rebuild its armaments and reputation, combine gunblades, magic, and relics, then investigate threats in the shadows of the Empire. A protector may also install a puppet in the name of restoring order; religious and political turns make the oath more than a simple promise of loyalty.
player_overview.recommended_for: Players who enjoy imperial politics, magical knights, and stories of protectors in danger of becoming something else.
signature_features: Imperial duty and freedom of action remain in tension throughout the campaign.
Gunblades, hybrid magic, and precursor relics are brought together.
Protecting the people and coercive political intervention define different value phases.
player_overview.tagline: Guard the Empire with magic and gunblades, then decide whether oath, people, or faith comes first.

phase_scores.phase: The Second Son's coercive political route

positive_indicators: Improves local safety and prosperity by pursuing bread, security, and prosperity.
values.rationale: Protecting those unable to defend themselves and seeking popular support through safety and prosperity are positive evidence. The Second Son event kills an occupied ruler and heir, installs a puppet, and imposes vassalage. Dangerous relics, theocracy, militarization, and war are not deductions by themselves. The later religious state is conditional and is not every player's inevitable route.
red_flags: The Second Son event kills the local ruler and heir.
Forcibly installs a new ruler and controls the resulting vassal.
